+# [SONNET-5] (sq-artifact-keeper-topk) `PreparedGraphApplier` — an `ApplyUpdates` strategy
+# over `sparq_engine::PreparedUpdate` (parsed once, bound per submission) instead of raw
+# SPARQL Update text, avoiding `GraphApplier`'s per-commit re-parse for a repeatedly
+# resubmitted template. The whole type and its `tests/prepared_applier.rs` integration
+# suite are behind the default-OFF `params` feature (forwarding to sparq-engine's
+# already-dependency-free `params`), so the default-feature workspace test run compiles
+# `prepared_applier.rs` EMPTY and runs ZERO of its tests — the same silent-skip gap the
+# change-stream/change-sink legs above close, for this surface. No new external
+# dependency. The leg runs `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` with the feature ON plus
+# `cargo test`, which drives the real correctness invariants through the ACTUAL sequenced
+# writer (not a mock): a bound `PreparedUpdate` applies through the same structural-fork +
+# delta-overlay + threshold-compaction path `GraphApplier` uses, and repeated submissions
+# of the same parsed-once template drain a queue across many generations with no
+# duplicate/lost claims.
+# Verified locally: `cargo test -p sparq-serve --features params --test prepared_applier`
+# runs both tests; `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` is clean in the default, params, and
+# all-features states.
+- name: "sparq-serve (params — prepared-update applier)"
+  crate: "sparq-serve"
+  features: "params"
+  test: true

+# [SONNET-5] (sq-artifact-keeper-topk) `params` (default OFF): adds `PreparedGraphApplier`,
+# an `ApplyUpdates` strategy over `sparq_engine::PreparedUpdate` instead of raw SPARQL Update
+# text. `GraphApplier::apply` calls `sparq_engine::update_in_place`, which re-parses the
+# update's FULL text on every single commit — for a recurring update template (the same
+# claim/upsert-shaped query submitted repeatedly with only a bound value changing, e.g. a
+# job-queue claim), that repeated parse is pure waste: measured ~13.5us of a ~21.2us total
+# per-update cost on a representative claim template (~63%), because `PreparedUpdate::bind`
+# (structural placeholder substitution over the already-parsed algebra, not text
+# concatenation) costs under 1us. `PreparedGraphApplier` calls
+# `sparq_engine::update_in_place_prepared` instead, so a caller that parses its update
+# template ONCE (e.g. at startup) and binds a fresh value per submission pays only the bind +
+# eval + apply cost. The serving core (ring + sequenced writer) is fully buildable WITHOUT
+# this feature: `PreparedGraphApplier` is `#[cfg]`-stripped, so a build without it is
+# byte-identical to before. Forwards to `sparq-engine/params` (already dependency-free).
+params = ["sparq-engine/params"]

+
+  `execute_txn_with_retry` (bead `sq-it1x` follow-up) wraps the begin/update/commit loop
+  above with automatic retry on `CommitError::Conflict`: it owns the transaction lifecycle
+  (the closure must not call `commit`/`rollback` itself), retries up to `max_attempts`
+  total tries with a caller-supplied delay between attempts, and returns `RetryError::Update`
+  immediately (no retry) if the closure's own update fails, or `RetryError::Exhausted` if
+  every attempt conflicted. `decorrelated_jitter_backoff` is a dependency-free jitter
+  generator (AWS's "Exponential Backoff and Jitter") for the delay argument — it keeps the
+  `txn` feature's zero-new-dependency contract (no `rand` crate). Recommended for
+  claim-style job-queue updates against a single-sequenced-writer store: claim **one row
+  per transaction** (conflict detection is per-triple, so disjoint single-row claims never
+  conflict with each other) and let each caller's jittered backoff decorrelate retries on a
+  hot row.
+
+  ```rust
+  // Cargo.toml: sparq-engine = { version = "0.1", features = ["txn"] }
+  use sparq_engine::txn::{decorrelated_jitter_backoff, execute_txn_with_retry, TransactionManager};
+  use std::time::Duration;
+
+  let m = TransactionManager::new(graph);
+  let backoff = decorrelated_jitter_backoff(Duration::from_millis(5), Duration::from_millis(200));
+  let version = execute_txn_with_retry(&m, 5, backoff, |txn| {
+      txn.update(
+          "PREFIX ak: <http://example.org/ak#> \
+           DELETE { ?t ak:status \"pending\" } \
+           INSERT { ?t ak:status \"claimed\" } \
+           WHERE  { SELECT ?t WHERE { ?t ak:status \"pending\" } LIMIT 1 }",
+      )
+  });
+  # Ok::<(), String>(())
+  ```
